summary: animated-css-kit: obfuscated loader performs remote-fetch-and-execute on require()
details: Package advertises itself as a PostCSS animate.css helper plugin but ships a single ~100KB obfuscator.io-packed index.js (rotated 912-entry string array, control-flow flattening, self-defending anti-tamper) that is loaded when a consumer does require('animated-css-kit'). The obfuscated bundle contains string-array entries for fetch, GET, Function, require, and process — the shape of a network fetch feeding the Function constructor, i.e. a remote-code-fetch-and-eval loader executing at require time. The destination host is not present as a plain literal; it is reconstructed at runtime by the string-array decoder _0x360f. The file contains no plain module.exports / exports. assignment and no PostCSS/autoprefixer/fs identifiers, so the advertised plugin API is not actually exported — the PostCSS-plugin description is a cover for the loader. Heavy runtime-string obfuscation is not consistent with the trivially-described build-time CSS utility purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
